title: Verifiable training: learning program execution from executor rewards only
question: Trained only on the executor's right/wrong signal for its own sampled answer (no answer labels, no self-grading), how close do a Transformer and the step-aligned latent program model get to their supervised versions, in and out of distribution?

predictions.PASS: reward-only training reaches >= 80% of supervised accuracy ID and OOD for the latent program model, and learns at all (>= 20% vs 10% chance)
predictions.R3: reported: the step-aligned model beats the Transformer under reward-only training by >= 5 points OOD
predictions.reward: 1 if the sampled answer equals the executor's result, else 0; REINFORCE with a running-mean baseline and 0.01 entropy bonus

prior_art: REINFORCE (Williams 1992), RL from verifiable rewards on math/code (e.g. 2110.14168 verifiers; outcome-reward RL), CLRS 2205.15659
not_claimed: Policy-gradient training from outcome rewards is prior art; the question is whether latent step-aligned execution learns from it on this benchmark.
